newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude market holds bullish mood, paper firme.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude market holds bullish mood, paper firme.

text.p: A bullish tone prevailed in the North Sea crude market on Tuesday, reflected in the Brent cash market if not in physical trade.
"Everyone feels quite bullish although it's been very quiet on the wet side," said one trader.
Brent intermonth spreads held early gains, with July/August traded again at -20 cents in the afternoon and August/September climbing to trade at -13 cents.

CFDs were also stronger, with next week (June 23-27) jumping more than 10 cents to trade at August Brent -36 cents and -34 cents. Gains on later weeks were smaller, almost wiping out the short-term market contango.
Outright Brent values eased off early highs which took August to $18.32 on the IPE screen and $18.27 on the paper market. August Brent was trading 24 cents up at $18.10 a barrel at 1741 GMT.

The physical market was quiet, with one Brent cargo loading June 26-28 traded at August Brent -60 cents, five cents weaker than two much deals on Monday. Some traders attributed the fall to the promptish loading dates.
The sole Brent date, loading July 2-4, nominated from the paper chains on Monday was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by Stasco, traders said.
July loading programmes, the last of which were released on Tuesday, scheduled a 190,000 barrel per day (bpd) increase in liftings from June.
The hike in volumes was mostly due to heavy field maintenance in July, and was in line with most traders' expectations.
"It's not far off with what we expected," said one trader.

The figures failed to dampen the bullish mood, with loadings still 70,000 bpd off May levels and concerns over production problems at fields in the Forties system, which has already knocked cargoes out of the June programme and led to a thin early July programme.
